pharm: Lipophilic dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that preferentially acts on cerebral vasculature to reduce vasospasm-related ischemic deficits after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.

Take on empty stomach - >=1 h before or 2 h after meals; avoid grapefruit juice
Use only if clearly needed; limited human data
Avoid; nimodipine and metabolites pass into human milk
Use with caution; monitor blood pressure
Reduce dose to 30 mg every 4 hours in cirrhosis; monitor BP/heart rate closely
Avoid; additive hypotension and CNS effects
Blood pressure, heart rate, neurologic status; correct enteral route only
summary: Nimodipine is a cerebroselective dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker indicated to improve neurological outcome by reducing the incidence and severity of ischemic deficits in patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage from ruptured intracranial berry aneurysms (Hunt and Hess Grades I-V). It is given orally or by feeding tube as 60 mg every 4 hours for 21 consecutive days, started within 96 hours of hemorrhage. It carries a BOXED WARNING that it must NEVER be administered intravenously or by any parenteral route - inadvertent IV administration has caused deaths and serious life-threatening events. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated because of the risk of profound hypotension.
indications: Improvement of neurological outcome by reducing the incidence and severity of ischemic deficits in patients with subarachnoid hemorrhage from ruptured intracranial berry aneurysms (Hunt and Hess Grades I to V)

dosage.d: 60 mg (two 30 mg capsules) every 4 hours for 21 consecutive days
dosage.n: Begin within 96 hours of onset; swallow whole >=1 h before or 2 h after meals
Monitor blood pressure and heart rate closely

dosage.c: Unable to swallow / via NG tube
dosage.d: Extract capsule contents into an oral/enteral syringe (NOT IV), give via NG/PEG tube, then flush with 30 mL normal saline
dosage.n: Label syringe Not for IV Use; never use a needle-compatible syringe

admin: ORAL OR ENTERAL ONLY - DO NOT administer intravenously or by any parenteral route (boxed warning)
Swallow capsules whole with a little liquid, preferably not less than 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals

If unable to swallow, puncture both ends of the capsule with an 18-gauge needle, extract the liquid into an ORAL syringe (one that cannot accept a needle), give via NG/PEG tube, and flush with normal saline
Label any administration syringe Not for IV Use; avoid grapefruit juice
Start as soon as possible within 96 hours of subarachnoid hemorrhage and continue for 21 days
moa: Nimodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that inhibits the influx of calcium ions through voltage-gated L-type channels into vascular smooth muscle and neurons. Its high lipophilicity allows it to cross the blood-brain barrier and act preferentially on cerebral arteries. By reducing calcium entry, it relaxes cerebral vascular smooth muscle and is thought to reduce the ischemic neuronal damage and vasospasm associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage.

absolute: Concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, telithromycin; HIV protease inhibitors such as ritonavir, indinavir, nelfinavir, saquinavir; azole antifungals such as ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole; nefazodone) - risk of significant hypotension
Intravenous or other parenteral administration (boxed warning - deaths reported)
relative: Concomitant other antihypertensives or CYP3A4 inhibitors

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; animal studies have shown adverse fetal effects. Nimodipine should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Nimodipine and its metabolites have been detected in human milk at concentrations similar to maternal plasma; breastfeeding is not recommended while taking nimodipine.
renal: Use with caution in patients with impaired renal function; monitor blood pressure carefully. Adverse events have been reported in patients with abnormal renal function.
hepatic: Patients with hepatic cirrhosis have markedly higher nimodipine exposure; the dose should be reduced to 30 mg every 4 hours with close monitoring of blood pressure and heart rate.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, telithromycin, ritonavir and other HIV protease inhibitors, ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, nefazodone) - CONTRAINDICATED; markedly increase nimodipine and cause severe hypotension
Other antihypertensives and IV beta-blockers - additive hypotension
moderate: Moderate/weak CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., erythromycin, fluoxetine, diltiazem, verapamil, valproic acid) - increase nimodipine; monitor blood pressure
CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital) - decrease nimodipine; may reduce efficacy
minor: Cimetidine - may modestly increase nimodipine plasma levels
interactions.food: Take on an empty stomach (>=1 hour before or 2 hours after meals).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; alcohol may potentiate hypotension and CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Grapefruit juice inhibits CYP3A4 and increases nimodipine levels - must be avoided.

serious: Worsening cerebral ischemia from excessive blood pressure reduction
Death and serious adverse events if administered intravenously
emergency: Profound hypotension with cardiovascular collapse (especially after inadvertent IV administration)

monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate closely, especially at initiation and in cirrhosis
Neurologic status and signs of cerebral ischemia
Confirmation that the medication is given by the oral/enteral route only
Hepatic function in patients with liver disease
counsel: This medicine is taken by mouth or feeding tube only - it must never be given into a vein
Take on an empty stomach, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals, and avoid grapefruit juice
Take every 4 hours for the full 21 days even if you feel well
Report dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, which may indicate low blood pressure
Tell all providers about this medicine before any new prescription, especially antifungals, certain antibiotics, and HIV medicines
pk: Absorption begins promptly; effect within hours of oral dosing
Dosed every 4 hours to maintain levels over 21 days
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions 15-30 C; protect capsules from light and freezing
pearls: BOXED WARNING: NEVER give intravenously or by any parenteral route - deaths and life-threatening events have occurred when capsule contents were injected
If patient cannot swallow, use only an ORAL syringe (cannot accept a needle), label it Not for IV Use, give via NG/PEG and flush with saline
Cerebroselective dihydropyridine - the only CCB proven to improve outcomes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
Start within 96 hours of hemorrhage; continue 60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days
Contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; avoid grapefruit juice; reduce dose in cirrhosis
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the every-4-hour schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose would be expected to cause cardiovascular effects such as excessive peripheral vasodilation with marked systemic hypotension. Clinically significant hypotension may require active cardiovascular support with pressor agents, and specific calcium channel blocker overdose treatments (e.g., intravenous calcium, high-dose insulin therapy) should be given promptly. Because nimodipine is highly protein-bound, dialysis is not likely to be beneficial. Inadvertent IV administration is a medical emergency.
